```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

A reference for every file a run can write. A typical run on eight samples
produces around twenty tables and twenty figures.

## Read these first

| File | Why |
|---|---|
| `recon_diagnostics.png` | Where every cut-off landed, sample by sample |
| `gating_qc.png` | The same, drawn on the distributions the cut-offs came from |
| `staining_qc.csv` | Which samples were dropped, and why |
| `thresholds_used.csv` | Every cut-off, and whether it found a clean dip or had to guess |

These four tell you whether the cells were divided up sensibly. If they were not,
nothing further down is worth reading, however good the p-values look.

## Populations and intensity

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `population_frequencies.csv` | What percentage each cell type makes up, per sample |
| `population_marker_mfi.csv` | How brightly each protein is expressed in each cell type, per sample, as both a median and a percentage of positive cells |
| `functional_markers.csv` | The same for any activation or exhaustion markers your config groups together |
| `population_ratios.csv` | Ratios such as CD4 to CD8, if your config asks for them |
| `gate_counts.csv` | How many cells survived each cleanup step |
| `population_frequencies.png` | Frequencies across all samples together |
| `population_marker_heatmap.png` | Proteins against cell types, so you can check the labels match the biology |

One warning about the `count` column. It is the number of cells recorded, which
depends on how long the machine ran, so it is not a measure of how many cells the
person has. Use `pct_of_cd45_pos` unless you supplied real counts from a blood
test.

## The embedding

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `cells_umap.csv` | One row per embedded cell with coordinates, sample, population |
| `umap_overview.png` | The embedding coloured by population and by sample |
| `umap_markers.png` | One panel per marker |
| `umap_density.png` | Where cells are concentrated |
| `umap_density_by_group.png` | The same, split by study group |
| `umap_overview_by_group.png` | Combined view plus one column per group |
| `umap_multigraph_overlay.png` | Per compartment marker curves against the reference group |
| `umap.model`, `umap.model.meta.rds` | Saved model, written by `--save-umap-model` |

The saved model lets a later batch be projected onto the same axes, so a cluster
stays where it was between runs. Projection is refused when the new data is
missing markers the model used, because filling the gap with zeros would give
coordinates that look plausible and mean nothing.

## Statistics

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `group_comparison_stats.csv` | Abundance between groups, one row per population |
| `group_comparison.png` | The same as boxplots |
| `marker_state_stats.csv` | Differential state, per population and marker |
| `marker_state.png` | The same as boxplots |
| `functional_markers_stats.csv` | Functional marker blocks between groups |
| `population_ratios_stats.csv` | Declared ratios between groups |
| `compositional_clr_stats.csv` | The abundance tests repeated on centred log-ratios |
| `compositional_concordance.csv` | Which findings survive both, and which do not |
| `paired_comparison_stats.csv` | Paired design, written by `--paired-column` |
| `covariate_adjusted_stats.csv` | Rank ANCOVA, written by `--rank-ancova` |
| `subcluster_marker_shifts.csv` | Pooled-cell marker shifts per compartment, no p-values |

Every test here uses one value per sample. `subcluster_marker_shifts.csv` is the
exception and says so: it ranks shifts over pooled cells, carries no p-value, and
answers a different question from the tests above it.

## Diagnostics

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `threshold_drift_stats.csv`, `threshold_drift.png` | Whether a gate moved with group |
| `threshold_scale_qc.csv` | Thresholds far from their peers in the same panel |
| `confounding_diagnostics.csv` | Whether each covariate differs by group and tracks the outcome |
| `batch_mixing_stats.csv` | iLISI against a permutation null |
| `batch_group_confounding.csv` | Cramér's V between batch and group |
| `batch_diagnostic.png` | The same, drawn |
| `run_manifest.txt` | Everything needed to say what produced this folder |

## Clustering and learned gates

Written when you pass `--cluster` or `--explain-clusters`.

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `unsupervised_clusters.csv`, `.png` | Cluster assignment per cell |
| `cluster_gate_agreement_clusters.csv` | Per cluster: which label dominates, and how purely |
| `cluster_gate_agreement_populations.csv` | Per population: recovered as a cluster, or scattered |
| `subcluster_k_selection.csv` | Chosen k per population, from `--auto-subcluster-k` |
| `cluster_gate_proposals.csv` | Learned gating strategies with held-out metrics |
| `cluster_gate_polygons.csv` | The polygon vertices, so you can redraw them |
| `cluster_gate_strategy_<k>.png` | One figure per explained cluster |

## Other

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `patient_metadata_english.csv` | The patient table after column mapping and translation |
| `absolute_counts.csv`, `.png`, `_stats.csv`, `_raw.csv`, `_qc.png` | Written by `--absolute-counts` |
| `flowjo/` | UMAP-annotated FCS files, written by `--flowjo-export` |
| `config_derived.yaml` | Everything the run derived, written by `--write-config` |
| `sample_map_template.csv` | A blank sample map, written by `--write-sample-map` |

`--write-config` and `--write-sample-map` both derive what they need and then
stop, so neither can be combined with a full run.

The FlowJo export writes one pooled file, one per sample, and one per group. Open
`_ALL_SAMPLES.fcs`, plot UMAP-1 against UMAP-2, and decode the Population,
SampleID and CohortID channels with `population_codes.csv`.

## A note on failures

Every analysis added on top of the core pipeline runs after the primary outputs
are already on disk, and is wrapped so that a failure logs a warning naming the
analysis and leaves everything else alone. An addition that can destroy the thing
it was added to is not an addition.
